drafts.text:
Every time I try to predict the move, I pay for it.
Predicting feels smart. You get to be the guy who called it.
Reacting feels boring. You just wait and take what's actually there.
The market keeps paying the boring one, not the smart one.
drafts.why: Best-reach shape built from the highest-liked comment on your account this week. No question, citable last line, honest (doesn't claim consistent profit).
drafts.why_es: Formato de mayor alcance construido desde el comentario con más likes de tu cuenta esta semana. Sin pregunta, última línea citable, honesto (no presume ganancias constantes).

drafts.text:
I never flip sides when I'm fresh.
I flip after an hour of getting chopped, when I'm tired and I just want the day to be over.
That's not a read. That's me being done, pretending it's a decision.
The chart didn't change in that moment. I did.
drafts.why: Deep-engagement format, echoes your own winning Sep 1 post but sharper. Stakes are self-honesty, blames no one but the tired version of you.
drafts.why_es: Formato de engagement profundo, hace eco de tu propio post ganador del 1 sep pero más filoso. La apuesta es honestidad propia, no culpa a nadie salvo a tu versión cansada.

drafts.text:
Don't be like me.
On a 25k account there's no reason to risk enough to pass in two days.
But two days sounds better than two weeks. So I size up and call it confidence.
Then one bad candle takes all of it, and I act surprised.
It was never the candle. It was the size I chose so I wouldn't have to be patient.
drafts.source: FxGal (@sowhateh) comment on the MFF Rapid post
drafts.why: Turns a real pushback into self-accountability on your actual revenge-sizing leak. Blames impatience, not the market, no fabricated dollar figures.
drafts.why_es: Convierte un comentario de crítica real en autorresponsabilidad sobre tu fuga real de revenge-sizing. Culpa a la impaciencia, no al mercado, sin cifras inventadas.
